summary.text: A female patient aged 65 at therapy initiation in a retrospective regorafenib plus 5-FU case series had left-sided colon cancer (stage IV at diagnosis) with metastasis to peritoneal, ovaries, abdominal wall, liver. Comorbidities were osteoarthritis. The patient had a history of tumor resection and had received 5 listed prior systemic regimens, including FOLFOX + Avastin.
Combination therapy used regorafenib at 120 mg at initiation and 80 mg at last follow-up or discontinuation with 5-FU. Side effects reported: grade 1-2 hand-foot syndrome.
Best response was stable disease at 7 weeks. At last follow-up, 10 months from initiation per the table, the status was alive on therapy.

summary.text: A male patient aged 48 at therapy initiation in a retrospective regorafenib plus 5-FU case series had left-sided colon cancer (stage III at diagnosis) with metastasis to liver. Comorbidities were hypertension. The patient had a history of tumor resection and had received 4 listed prior systemic regimens, including Capecitabine+ Oxaliplatin.
Combination therapy used regorafenib at 80 mg at initiation and 120 mg at last follow-up or discontinuation with 5-FU received in an outside facility. Table 3 reports the treatment as well-tolerated.
Best response was partial response at 12 weeks. At last follow-up, 8.5 months from initiation per the table, the status was alive on therapy.

summary.text: A male patient aged 58 at therapy initiation in a retrospective regorafenib plus 5-FU case series had right-sided colon cancer (stage IV at diagnosis) with metastasis to liver, lung. Comorbidities were hypertension and diabetes mellitus. The patient had a history of tumor resection and had received 3 listed prior systemic regimens, including FOLFOX.
Combination therapy used regorafenib at 120 mg at initiation and 120 mg at last follow-up or discontinuation with 5-FU. Side effects reported: grade 3 hypertension.
Best response was progressive disease at 7 weeks. At last follow-up, 20 months from initiation per the table, the status was alive on other therapy.

summary.text: A male patient aged 58 at therapy initiation in a retrospective regorafenib plus 5-FU case series had left-sided colon cancer (stage IV at diagnosis) with metastasis to liver, lung. Comorbidities were hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. The patient had a history of tumor resection and had received 4 listed prior systemic regimens, including FOLFOX.
Combination therapy used regorafenib at 120 mg at initiation and 80 mg at last follow-up or discontinuation with 5-FU. Side effects reported: grade 1-2 mucositis.
Best response was progressive disease at 6 weeks. At last follow-up, 6 months from initiation per the table, the status was alive on other therapy.

summary.text: A male patient aged 59 at therapy initiation in a retrospective regorafenib plus 5-FU case series had rectal cancer (stage IV at diagnosis) with metastasis to liver, lung. Comorbidities were hypertension and gout. The patient had a history of tumor resection and had received 9 listed prior systemic regimens, including Capecitabine.
Combination therapy used regorafenib at 160 mg at initiation and 160 mg at last follow-up or discontinuation with 5-FU. Side effects reported: grade 3 pneumonitis.
Best response was stable disease at 7 weeks. At last follow-up, 2 months from initiation per the table, the status was deceased.

article_limitations: The article has no figures or supplements; all content comes from text and three per-patient tables (one row per segment).

Table cells for prior chemotherapies, mutations, comorbidities and subsequent therapies print several entries run together without separators; they were split by regimen or marker name and their sequence is not stated.

Series-level statements (ethnicity counts, unlabelled dose reductions, 5-FU dosing counts, imaging assessment, two patients with prior regorafenib monotherapy, MSI statement) are not attributed to individuals unless the sentence names the patient or covers all seven.
Table 2 progression/discontinuation time header gives no unit; the value 30 for patient 4 is not consistent with its 8-week progressive-disease best response and is kept review_only as an ambiguity.
Discussion text cites published cases and trials (Ma, Wang, Marks, Lin, Sanoff, CORDIAL, ReDOS) which are not patients of this series and are not annotated.
